questions.question: Q: What is the difference between the focus and epicentre of an earthquake?
questions.correctAnswer: The focus is the point underground where the earthquake originates. The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.

questions.question: Q: Why are volcanoes at subduction zones more explosive than those at mid-ocean ridges?
questions.correctAnswer: Subduction zone magma is andesitic/rhyolitic with higher silica, more viscosity, and trapped gas. Pressure builds until an explosive eruption occurs. Mid-ocean ridge magma is basaltic with lower silica, less viscosity, and gas escapes easily, producing gentle effusive eruptions.

questions.question: Q: Name three volcanic hazards and describe each.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Pyroclastic flow: fast-moving current of hot gas, ash and rock. 2) Lahar: volcanic mudflow of ash mixed with water. 3) Ash fall: fine volcanic particles ejected into the atmosphere and deposited over large areas.

questions.question: Q: What causes a tsunami?
questions.correctAnswer: A large displacement of water, typically caused by a submarine earthquake, volcanic eruption or landslide. The sudden movement of the seafloor pushes a column of water upward, generating waves that travel across the ocean at high speed.

questions.question: Q: How does liquefaction cause damage during an earthquake?
questions.correctAnswer: Earthquake shaking causes water-saturated, unconsolidated sediment to lose strength and behave like a liquid. Buildings and infrastructure can sink, tilt or collapse as the ground loses its ability to support loads.
